The World is Broken into Hexes

After the collapse of Adam Kadmon, reality did not simply shatter — it fragmented into structured pieces.

These pieces are called hexes.

Each hex is a region of the world containing its own:

• geography
• people
• dangers
• resources
• mysteries

When you look at the campaign map, each hex represents a fragment of reality waiting to be explored, understood, and repaired.

What a Hex Represents

A hex is not just a location.

It is a story container.

Every hex may contain:

• settlements or ruins
• natural resources
• strange phenomena
• hostile forces
• opportunities for development

Exploring hexes is one of the main ways players discover new problems to solve and new ways to improve the world.

Exploring Hexes

When your faction travels into a new hex, several things may happen.

You might:

• discover a hidden settlement
• uncover ancient infrastructure
• encounter hostile creatures
• trigger a Campaign Beat
• reveal corruption or Darkness

Exploration is the primary way the campaign map becomes alive and meaningful.

Developing Hexes

Once a hex is secured, your faction can begin improving it.

Development might include:

• building infrastructure
• restoring damaged facilities
• creating defensive structures
• integrating local communities

Over time, a developed hex becomes part of your faction’s territory and support network.

Hex Ownership and Territory

When your faction invests in a hex, it becomes part of your territory.

Controlled hexes provide:

• resources
• strategic positioning
• travel routes
• narrative influence

Protecting your territory becomes increasingly important as your faction grows.

Hex Connections

Hexes are connected to neighboring regions.

Movement between hexes allows factions to:

• explore new territory
• reach important locations
• respond to threats
• expand their influence

Travel between hexes may trigger encounters or reveal hidden dangers.

Hex Hazards

Not every hex is safe.

Some regions may contain:

• corrupted environments
• radiation zones
• magical anomalies
• hostile factions
• dangerous creatures

Entering hazardous hexes often creates new challenges for the players.

The Hex Development Cycle

Over time, hexes evolve as players interact with them.

A typical cycle looks like this:

Discover Hex
     ↓
Explore the Region
     ↓
Encounter Problems
     ↓
Resolve Conflicts
     ↓
Develop Infrastructure
     ↓
Integrate into Territory

As more hexes are developed, the world slowly becomes more stable and connected.

Hexes and the Great Work

Repairing hexes is one of the most important ways factions contribute to the Great Work.

Each restored region pushes reality a little closer to harmony.

Each neglected or corrupted hex pushes it further toward collapse.

Hex Strategy

As your faction grows, hex decisions become strategic.

You may choose to:

• expand into new regions
• secure important travel routes
• develop resource-rich hexes
• confront dangerous corruption

Every hex represents a choice about the future of the world.

What Players Should Remember

When thinking about hexes, remember three simple ideas:

1 — Hexes are places to explore

They contain mysteries and opportunities.

2 — Hexes are problems to solve

Every region has challenges that must be addressed.

3 — Hexes are foundations for growth

Developed hexes strengthen your faction and the world.

In Simple Terms

Hexes are the building blocks of the campaign world.

Exploring them reveals the story.

Developing them shapes the future.

And repairing them brings the world closer to completion.
